reference_calls.source_slice: On 5 December 1914 Endurance departed South Georgia,
on 15 April their lifeboats reached Elephant Island,
uninhabited rock far from shipping lanes.
On 24 April Shackleton and five others embarked in the James Caird,
on a perilous voyage of some 1,300 kilometres.
As ferocious gales battered the boat,
Worsley snatched only four sights of the sun,
deducing the rest by dead reckoning from course,
and Tom Crean traversed its mountainous interior in about 36 exhausting hours,
reaching the Stromness whaling station on 20 May.
Ice repelled three rescue attempts before the Yelcho,
evacuated the 22 marooned men on 30 August.
On 5 March 2022 searchers located the wreck 3,008 metres down,
She lay about four miles south of the spot Worsley recorded in November 1915,
a slight discrepancy for a calculation on shifting ice.
Precision put six ashore within reach of help and,
brought their ship back into view.
